records.name: Caraga
records.summary:
Caraga has no documented region-specific laws affecting transgender people; the national framework is what applies here: same-sex conduct is legal, there is no legal gender-recognition pathway, national SOGIE equality legislation has been filed since 1999 without enactment, and anti-discrimination ordinances exist only at some city and provincial levels. The Safe Spaces Act criminalises homophobic and transphobic slurs, school anti-bullying rules and gender-responsive education policy cover SOGI grounds, and executive orders created a national diversity-and-inclusion programme that, per audited reporting, remained unimplemented as of 2025.

Acceptance runs partial: a 2018 national survey recorded about one-fifth support for same-sex civil unions and majority opposition to trans women's use of women's toilets. A June 2025 report on the killing of an eighteen-year-old trans student, which a national alliance presented as part of a pattern of violence against trans Filipinas, originates in a different region — it is Caraga only as part of the archipelago-wide climate, and is recorded as exactly that.

records.summary: The dedicated country dossier found no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division, so it was assessed at the national score (±0.02). The 2025 Movilh annual report places Antofagasta at 2.09% of nationally documented abuse cases — up from 1.32% in 2024 — with a +45.45% year-on-year rise in 2025, the second-largest regional increase of any region, inside a national pattern where only the two biggest regions fell while the other 14 rose (national total 3,620 cases, +27.1%, a 24-year record). The dossier's warning applies: a mid-share reading here reflects documented hate diffusing into lower-visibility territories rather than safety.

records.summary: The dedicated country dossier found no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division, so it was assessed at the national score (±0.02). The 2025 Movilh annual report places Atacama at 1.83% of nationally documented abuse cases (1.56% in 2024) with a +7.69% year-on-year rise in 2025 — inside a national pattern where only the two biggest regions fell while the other 14 rose (national total 3,620 cases, +27.1%, a 24-year record). Local institutional movement was positive: the Municipality of Atacama convened the commune's first Pride march, and one of the 2025 pride marches that expanded the movement's territorial visibility was held here.

records.name: RegiÃ³n de AysÃ©n del Gral.IbaÃ±ez del Campo
records.summary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 0.48% (Movilh regional table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year.

There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression since the return of democracy. Protective national framework (Gender Identity Law 21.120 in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, anti-discrimination law 21.220) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (PAIG excluded from the 2026 budget; health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors; legislative initiative CEI-57) and administrative document friction from Registro Civil identification-system issuance failures (Comptroller Final Report 264/2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.
